templates.text: The world is first understood as a shifting mosaic of light and shadow, with high-contrast edges drawing the earliest focus.
Perception anchors to the stark geometry of a caregiver's face, tracing the dark triangle of eyes and mouth against a luminous background.
Reality is parsed through the dance of luminance, where a slowly moving {object} becomes the primary object of rapt, silent attention.
The infant's awareness flows along visual contours, following lines and curves before comprehending the whole form.
Existence is a grainy, close-focus tableau where the blur of a cheek and the sharp line of a jaw define safety.
Consciousness is drawn like a magnet to areas of maximal contrast, building the world from patches of black, white, and red.
The environment is a soft-focus stage where any sudden lateral motion triggers an orienting response, head turning to track.
Understanding begins with the slow tracking of a complex pattern, a cognitive grip found in visual persistence.
The world is a luminous fog, with human faces emerging as the first coherent, compelling structures to be studied.
Perception is a hungry scan for edges, building stability from the intersecting lines of a crib or a window frame.
Awareness pools in the region of sharpest focus, approximately {distance} inches away, where details first cohere into meaning.
Experience is fundamentally chromatic, with a primal attraction to the saturated warmth of red hues over cooler tones.
The infant maps reality through the predictable oscillation of a mobile, learning rhythm and recurrence through sight.
Consciousness is visual pursuit; what the eyes can follow and fixate upon becomes real and worthy of attention.
The world assembles itself from fragmented glimpses, with the repeated sight of a primary caregiver forming the core schema.
Perception is anchored by looming stimuli, where an approaching face triggers a stilling response and intense visual inspection.
Understanding unfolds in the silent language of gaze, where shared visual attention lays the groundwork for connection.
Reality is a high-contrast sketchbook, with the bold stripes of a blanket providing more cognitive nourishment than pastel plains.
The infant's mind is a camera obscura, where the inverted, blurry image of a world slowly gains focus and organization.
Awareness is synonymous with visual novelty; a familiar shape holds attention for {seconds} seconds before a new contour beckons.
Existence is parsed through the aperture of central vision, with peripheral movement serving only as a trigger to re-center.
The foundational sense is one of visual rhythm, finding patterns in the periodic swing of a door or the pulse of a light.
The world is first a study in positive and negative space, learning object from background through edges and occlusion.
Perception is a hungry, scanning saccade, building a mental map from a series of fixations on points of high interest.
Consciousness brightens with increasing ambient light, with alertness and visual engagement peaking in well-lit spaces.
Understanding is rooted in the constancy of objects that remain visually present, even when partially hidden.
The infant navigates by visual landmarks—the dark square of a picture frame, the patterned blur of a curtain.
Reality gains dimension through motion parallax, as closer objects sweep by faster during a turn of the head.
Awareness is captivated by biological motion, the specific, fluid movement of a human form against a static background.
The world coheres where light meets dark, building a universe from the fundamental dialogue of shadow and illumination.
